_source: MITC MEGA HOME EXPO AUGUST 2026 (28/08/26 - 31/08/26) Price List
_transcribed: Read from the supplied PDF, rendered at 300dpi. Every rate below was read off the table; none was inferred. Open readings are listed in SPEC.md section 13 under A13.
_editable: This file is the price list. It is hand-editable and is the ONLY place rates live. Changing a price here changes the app, with no code change and no rebuild of anything but the asset.

promo.note: Fair rates. These ARE the printed fair prices, not a discount applied to a standard list. The standard list is still outstanding - SPEC.md section 13, A3.

config._einvoice: SPEC.md section 10.2-10.4. Malaysian law, not this shop's policy: since 1 Jan 2026 a single transaction above RM10,000 needs its own e-invoice and cannot go into a monthly consolidated batch. Config rather than code because section 10.3 says it will change, and because a change to it must reach every handset the way a price change does - by publishing a card, with no rebuild.
config._einvoice_prompt: Section 10.4's timing trap. The fair estimate is rough and an order quoted at RM8,500 settles at RM11,200, so the quote wizard asks from RM8,000 - while the customer is still standing there. The margin applies to the estimate only; a final is exact and needs none.
config._plausible_dimensions: SPEC.md section 5.4. What size a thing can physically be, per deposit category and per dimension, in tenths of a millimetre. Config rather than hardcoded guesses: a plausible curtain drop is not a plausible floor length. These are DELIBERATELY GENEROUS - they exist to catch 8000in (203 metres), not to second-guess a real order. A warning that fires on real work is a warning staff learn to tap past. A category absent from this map warns on nothing, which is the safe default: a missing config must never invent a limit that blocks a real order.
config._plausible_second_dimension: The SECOND dimension is named for what it actually is, because whoever edits this file has to recognise it. A curtain hangs, so it has a DROP. A floor lies flat, so it has a LENGTH - it is not a height, and asking a part-timer standing in a room for the 'height' of a floor invites them to type the wall. Wallpaper covers a wall, so it really is a HEIGHT. Use drop_/length_/height_ to match the category; the loader reads whichever is present.
